text:
Last night's Integration Debt Night at Kestrelmoor's Flatiron office was one of the more useful panels I've been to this year. About 60 of us packed in to hear Priya Raman-Holt (VP Platform, Tallowbrook) and Marcus Feldane (founder, Quillary) talk about the unglamorous work that decides whether AI actually ships.

A few things stuck with me:

→ Tallowbrook maintains 140 partner integrations with a team of three engineers. Priya's explanation: "We stopped building connectors one by one and started publishing a spec. Partners build to it now."

→ Marcus argued that agent pilots fail at the integration seam, not at the model. His team's rule: wire up data access before choosing a model.

→ Then a show of hands: about 40 of the 60 in the room said an agent pilot at their company had stalled on getting data access. That number says a lot.

The best moment was a disagreement. Priya thinks partners should own their connectors. Marcus thinks the platform has to own them or quality drifts. I left without a clear winner, and I think the answer depends on how much you can afford to police.

My takeaway for anyone selling or buying AI: ask about the data plumbing before you ask about the model.

Thanks to the Kestrelmoor team for hosting.

Where has your pilot stalled: the model or the access?
